item.title: Blues 'going to need a bit more killer instinct'
item.description: [BBC] Prior to Tuesday night's kick-off, the news that both August Priske and James Beadle were out was slightly concerning. Most of Millwall's team are over six feet tall and we would need as much height in the squad as possible, In the event, Alex Cochrane magnificently knocked them off their stride with less than a minute on the clock; I can't remember the last time we scored that quickly. The whole of the first half was a comprehensive dismantling of a team that were only a few points behind us in the table. If there was a fly in the ointment at all, it was that we seemed to take our foot off the gas in the second half. If we really are going to make a concerted attack on the top of the table, we're going to need a bit more killer instinct. The stats show that the promoted teams consistently score a lot of goals, so we have to keep working on our attacking play. On the goals conceded side, we're doing really well and fingers crossed, there won't be any injuries or suspensions for Christoph Klarer and Phil Neumann. I can't help feeling a bit sorry for Dael Fry though; he's barely seeing the light of day at the moment. Something that is really helping us at the moment is the quality of the players we can put on the wing. Liam Millar and Patrick Roberts are currently first choice, but Carlos Vicente and Demarai Gray are well capable of continuing the pressure on opposition defenders when they are subbed on. And once again, a shoutout for Jay Stansfield. He got the goal he has been craving and it was great to hear the ground erupt with his name. He contributes so much to the press in every game, and had two really good opportunities on Saturday. It's one of those three-game weeks again, so can we get nine points out of nine? Swansea are going to be a tough opponent on Saturday; they slipped up against Portsmouth on Tuesday and will want to put things right. Both of us are going to be looking for another three points to take into the international break. Hear and read more from Kym Smith on Birmingham Hospital Radio

item.title: Stephen A. Smith says there’s something wrong with Skip Bayless after his Chicago Bears claim
item.description: Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for SiriusXM Stephen A. Smith has taken aim at Skip Bayless after the veteran sports commentator backed Caleb Williams’ claim that Chicago has always been a Bears town, even during Michael Jordan’s time with the Bulls. The debate began after Williams said he had been told that the Bears remained more popular in Chicago than the Bulls during their dominant run in the 1990s. Bayless agreed with the quarterback, drawing on his experience as a Chicago Tribune columnist in 1998. However, Smith was far from convinced. Stephen A. Smith takes aim at Skip Bayless over Chicago Bears claim Bayless argued that the 1985 Bears remain more important to Chicago than Jordan’s Bulls, who won six NBA championships during the decade. Smith clearly disagreed with that assessment and did not hold back when addressing his former First Take colleague. In a pointed message, Smith said: “You must have been watching First Take because you posted this quote. Last night, Caleb Williams said, ‘Even during the Jordan era, Chicago was a Bears town.’ He’s right. I was the Chicago Tribune columnist in 1998. The 85 Bears were and still are bigger for more people in Chicago than even MJ’s NBA team. “The blasphemy, the criminal verbiage that you threw out there. I mean, if it wasn’t if it wasn’t for me knowing you the way that I do, I would ask for your diet Mountain Dew to be drug tested. Something’s wrong with you, but I will give you an opportunity to respond to the drivel you’re putting out there.” Smith’s reaction underlined just how strongly he disagrees with Bayless, even though the latter has first-hand experience covering Chicago during the Bulls’ championship era. The debate also comes after Williams’ comments drew criticism from Chris Canty, who questioned why the quarterback had brought Jordan into the conversation. However, Bayless defended Williams, while several fans also argued that the Bears have always held a special place in Chicago’s sporting culture. The 1985 Bears remain an iconic team in the city, but Jordan’s Bulls became a global phenomenon during their six-title run. For now, Bayless has been given an opportunity to respond to Smith’s criticism, with the disagreement adding another chapter to their long-running sports media rivalry. item.title: Ranji Trophy: Vijay Dahiya seeks accountability from tame Delhi
item.description: NEW DELHI: Delhi finished the first leg of this season’s Ranji Trophy with three points from an insipid draw against Services at the Air Force ground in Palam on Thursday. Services set them an improbable target of 320 from 56 overs on the last day after their captain Rajat Paliwal scored 116, his second century of the match. For a brief while it appeared Delhi were going after the target. After Priyansh Arya and Ayush Badoni fell for 15 and 17 respectively, everything seemed a formality even as Yash Dhull eased to an unbeaten 104 off 104 balls as Delhi’s Ranji campaign remained in tatters with seven points from four matches. Delhi’s red-ball cricket has been in a freefall for a while. Coach Vijay Dahiya spared no words to express his disappointment. Both of Delhi’s home matches finished in draws despite taking the early advantage. “When you want to win a game of a day’s cricket, you have to dictate terms. We didn’t dictate any session, and are disappointed because we wanted maximum out of this game to stay alive,” he said. Dahiya said the players need to be accountable. “The system is backing you. This year, there has been no wholesome changes despite a defeat. You have enough time if you are professional enough. That is one thing that is needed is taking accountability as an individual,” he said. The Delhi team has failed to seize the initiative. item.title: Football Player of the Week is Luke Bubnowski of Bernards for Week 9
item.description: After two straight trips to the sectional finals, the Bernards High School football team was severely disappointed last season when it was ousted in the opening round of the state tournament. Perhaps if the club had Luke Bubnowski as part of the backfield mix and starring at linebacker, things would have done differently. More: Pincus and Mendlowitz’s Big Central Conference playoff football picks Now, with his return after missing all of last season with an injury, Bubnowski had a huge impact in last weekend’s dramatic 21-20 victory over Hanover Park in the first round of the North 2 Group 2 Tournament. The senior not only rushed for 96 yards and all three touchdowns, but recorded 10 tackles, a sack and recovered two fumbles to send Bernards into a semifinals matchup this Friday night at Hoboken, earning MyCentralJersey.com Big Central Football Player of the Week honors. He’s rushed for 498 yards and seven touchdowns for the season, while delivering 56 tackles, the two recovered fumbles, and he returned an interception for a touchdown earlier this season. “Luke’s comeback this year after missing last year to the knee surgery has been a big part of why we have been able to be so successful,” Bernards coach Jon Simoneau said. “He’s come back bigger and stronger than he was before the injury, and to a level where he routinely plays well over a 100 snaps a game. item.description: Elliot Powell took over as Jersey Bulls manager in the summer of 2024 [Lauren Queree/Jersey Bulls] Jersey Bulls boss Elliot Powell says he would swap his Manager of the Month award for October for a league title win. Powell has earned the award by leading his unbeaten side to top of Isthmian League South Central after 15 games. The islanders - who have not lost in 34 league and play-off matches stretching back to last season - are a point clear of Bognor Regis Town, with a game in hand. "It's obviously a good testament to the work that we've done as a coaching team, and as a playing team as well," Powell told BBC Radio Jersey. "But there's other awards I'd prefer, and if I could swap one out for May time, I would do that right now. I'd bite your hand off for it. "It's nice to get recognised, but ultimately there's bigger prizes to be won and hopefully we'll be in the reckoning come May." Jersey Bulls suffer play-off heartbreak with shootout loss Jersey Bulls boss Powell may step down at end of season Powell's side have not lost a game outside of the FA Cup and FA Trophy since 30 December. But they came very close to defeat last Saturday when they needed a late equaliser to draw 1-1 with Hayes and Yeading United. Bulls travel to 16th-placed Hartley Wintney on Saturday in the first of three games against sides in the bottom seven before hosting title rivals Bognor Regis on 28 November. "The run that we're on, it is impressive and that always gives us a little bit of notice, but we want to keep that going," he said. "We want to take that to 35 games this weekend, and then we've got a couple of home games that are really important for us. item.title: Caitlin Clark Makes History With Major New Deal As WNBA Star Becomes First-Ever Face Of Two Retail Giants
item.description: Caitlin Clark has made history once again, this time away from the basketball court, after signing a groundbreaking multiyear partnership with DICK’S Sporting Goods and Foot Locker. The Indiana Fever superstar is officially the first athlete to become a brand partner for either retailer, marking another major milestone in her rapidly expanding business career. The exclusive agreement will see Clark appear in national and international campaigns, promote her signature footwear, and participate in fan events across both brands. For the 24-year-old WNBA star, the partnership is particularly meaningful because DICK’S was one of her favorite places to shop growing up. Caitlin Clark Makes History With First-Ever DICK’S And Foot Locker Deal ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Clark’s historic partnership was officially announced on November 4, making her the first individual athlete to sign a brand-level agreement with either DICK’S Sporting Goods or Foot Locker. According to the official company announcement , the exclusive multiyear deal will bring Clark’s brand to customers across the United States and internationally. The agreement includes national and global advertising campaigns, promotions for her signature footwear and apparel, in-store experiences, appearances, and community events. Although both retailers have previously collaborated with professional athletes, neither had signed an individual athlete as an official brand partner. The financial terms of Clark’s agreement have not been publicly disclosed. The partnership also marks an important development for DICK’S, which now owns Foot Locker and can promote Clark across both retail networks. item.description: Preview | Juventus Women-Sassuolo The Women's First Team host Sassuolo on Matchday 6 of the Serie A Women season, with the aim of building on the 2-1 win over Fiorentina at the start of the week. The clash will take place at 18:00 CET on Saturday, November 7. Let’s get up to speed ahead of the game with the pre-match stats. INTERESTING FACTS Juventus are unbeaten in 19 of their 20 Serie A matches against Sassuolo, with 15 wins and four draws – the only exception being their defeat in March 2019 away to the Neroverdi. Only against Fiorentina (13) have Juventus kept more clean sheets in Serie A than against Sassuolo (10). Juventus and Sassuolo are the two teams with the worst defences in this league, having conceded 13 and 11 goals respectively so far. The Neroverdi have also conceded the most shots from opponents, both in total (92) and on target (34). Alba Redondo has scored four goals in the first five matchdays of this Serie A season – at least double that of any other teammate – and could become only the third foreign player to score at least five in the Bianconeri’s first six league matches of the season, after Eniola Aluko and Lineth Beerensteyn. On only three occasions so far have the Neroverdi found themselves with two points or fewer after the first six league matches of the season: in 2017/18 (0), in 2022/23 (one) and in 2024/25 (one). item.title: The Bayern Insider: Martin Odegaard rumour as Eberl dreams of Antonio Nusa
item.description: The Bayern Insider: Martin Odegaard rumour as Eberl dreams of Antonio Nusa Welcome to today’s exclusive & comprehensive round-up of all things Bayern Munich from Bayern insider Christian Falk. Featuring updates on Rio Ngumoha, Martin Odegaard, Antonio Nusa, and Tomas Araujo. Today’s top stories Could Antonio Nusa or Jadon Sancho be arriving in January at Bayern Munich to help out on the left wing? Were Bayern closer to signing Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha than everyone initially thought? Could Arsenal’s Martin Ødegaard be the next Premier League expert to Munich? And plenty more on Nick Woltemade, Lennart Karl, Ismael Saibari & JJ Gabriel It’s very good news that Harry Kane has extended his contract until 2029. Kane himself made no secret of the fact that he wanted this contract extension – and Bayern were all too happy to supply it. As we reported previously, it will be a contract until 2029. It’s really interesting what’s in this contract; there were many rumours about whether or not Tottenham have a matching right or a buy-back option, but I can now confirm that it’s not true that either is in the contract. There was no Ballon d’Or clause included in the contract either. I’m sorry, Spurs fans, but the Tottenham connection is fully over. Kane is now a Bayern Munich player. There are some clauses included in the hopes that he’ll continue to score a mountain of goals for FC Bayern. He has a Ballon d’Or clause (and can earn more than €1m as he did this year), a golden shoe clause, best striker in the Bundesliga, best striker in the Champions League, and so on. Harry Kane wants to score many goals for Bayern Munich – and he has a contract that will reward him for this. Want more CF Bayern Insider coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Bayern beat Atletico Madrid at the Metropolitano (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) It was a really interesting game. You have to bear in mind the squad Bayern had going into the fixture with Atletico Madrid. Luis Diaz is still injured, Saibari injured, Gnabry injured, and Musiala injured. So, not quite the best possible front line FC Bayern could put out in Madrid. Yet, these guys stuck together, also without Vincent Kompany (who’ll be out of action until the international break), and got the win. I’ve often been in Madrid back when Atletico were at their old stadium, the Calderón, and I’ve been at their new one, the Metropolitano. It was always hard for Bayern Munich. Nonetheless, they did an incredible job this week. I think they could build up to something very special in the Champions League this season, because you can see everyone is fighting for each other and the shirt. Bayern have generally tended to play well against Atletico, but it would often be the case that Atletico were just that bit more aggressive. The Northamptonshire-based side, backed by the late Max Griggs, rocketed through non-league in the 1990s and in 2003 reached the third tier of English football before financial issues after he stepped away ultimately saw them fold. A community lost its focal point, and within years their Nene Park stadium had been razed to the ground. Usher, like many of those involved with the Northern Premier League Division One Midlands side, has followed both incarnations of the club - firstly as a fan, but also as a groundsman and turnstile operator before becoming chairman in 2022. "My first game was an FA Cup tie against Shrewsbury Town in 1998. It was the year we ended up playing Leeds United in the third round." he said. "Rushden & Diamonds gave us some great times. item.description: Darian Mensah's NFL Draft projection: Why Heisman front-runner isn't higher on 2027 draft boards originally appeared on The Sporting News . The 2026 college football season began with expectations that it might preview one of the strongest NFL quarterback classes in recent memory. Instead, the perceived top prospects have been all over the map. Arch Manning and Dante Moore have slid, while Drew Mestemaker has surged and CJ Carr has held steady. No one might be having a better season than Miami's Darian Mensah, though. Mensah has 25 touchdowns to just one interception through eight games, completing more than 80 percent of passes and positioning himself as a Heisman Trophy front-runner. Still, not all NFL front offices are sold on Mensah's status as a high first-round pick. Here's a closer look at Mensah's NFL Draft stock and why he isn't ranked higher. ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. ranks Mensah fourth among all prospects in 2027, while Sporting News' own Vinnie Iyer doesn't have Mensah in the first round of his most recent NFL mock draft . CBS Sports , meanwhile, ranks Mensah 81st among all prospects, signaling how many different opinions exist about the Miami quarterback. If half of NFL teams view him as a legitimate first-round prospect and half don't, odds are Mensah is going to land on the higher end of that spectrum. All it takes is one team to believe in a quarterback for that quarterback to come off the board early, and Mensah's production has been so dominant that it wouldn't be surprising to see him land near the top of the first round. Here are the details behind Mensah's inconsistent draft stock. Why isn't Darian Mensah higher on draft boards? As a player, Mensah's arm strength is a potential red flag for NFL teams. Mensah's ball placement has easily made up for solid but unspectacular arm strength at the college level, but NFL teams will have to evaluate whether they believe that will stand up at the next level. The inconsistent evaluations of Mensah might also be related to Miami's schedule this season. The Hurricanes simply haven't faced many high-level defenses, making it tougher to evaluate his decision-making. That is set to change, of course, as Miami will face Notre Dame and should be in line for at least one big-time matchup in the College Football Playoff. If Mensah can come close to sustaining his production against tougher competition, he might win over some skeptical evaluators. item.description: Liverpool star called up to national team for UEFA Nations League fixtures Giorgi Mamardashvili in Georgia Squad for Key Nations League Matches Georgia have named a 26-man squad for their final UEFA Nations League fixtures of the 2026/27 campaign, and for Liverpool supporters the headline is simple, Giorgi Mamardashvili is in. Ramaz Svanadze’s side face Hungary in Tbilisi on 14 November before meeting Ukraine in Košice three days later. There are three new faces in the group, Dinamo Batumi goalkeeper Nodar Kalichava, Polissya defender Giorgi Maisuradze and Spartak Trnava midfielder Giorgi Moistrapishvili. Fresh blood was needed, and Svanadze has brought it in without ripping up the core. Georgia Squad Built Around Mamardashvili Mamardashvili remains one of the central figures in this Georgia squad. He has 42 caps already, which tells you plenty about his standing despite still being only 26. Since his debut against Bulgaria in September 2021, he has moved quickly from promising goalkeeper to one of the first names on the teamsheet. That status was cemented at Euro 2024. His 21 group-stage saves were the joint-most recorded by any goalkeeper in the tournament’s history. It was not decorative goalkeeping, it was survival-level work, done repeatedly under pressure. He also collected Georgian Footballer of the Year in 2024, ending Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s sequence of wins. That matters, because awards can be noisy, but this one reflected his actual influence. item.title: Virgil van Dijk admits Liverpool's defensive struggles are 'not sustainable'
item.description: Virgil van Dijk admits Liverpool's defensive struggles are 'not sustainable' Virgil van Dijk has warned that Liverpool 's defensive record is 'not sustainable' after Fenerbahce scored three times from set-pieces to beat the Reds 3-2 in Istanbul. Andoni Iraola's side led twice in the Champions League on Wednesday, through Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak, but were pegged back quickly on both occasions before Vedat Muriqi headed a 79th-minute winner. The defeat ended Liverpool's perfect record in this season's league phase, but the worry runs deeper than one result. The Reds had also let in three goals in their wins over Villarreal and LASK, the first time Liverpool have ever conceded three or more in three consecutive major European games. It also means back-to-back defeats for the first time under Iraola, following the loss to Arsenal at the weekend. Liverpool's league record makes for better reading, with only three teams having conceded fewer than their nine goals. However, Van Dijk warned his team that their concession of soft goals cannot continue in Europe. "It's definitely not sustainable. That's why it's a very disappointing night for many reasons, but definitely because of the goals we conceded and the manner we conceded them as well. There is work to do." - Virgil van Dijk The captain singled out the set-piece goals as the most frustrating part of the night. "Three set-pieces as well. We have been very good at them so far this season, but we switched off and weren't ready for the first and second balls. It's a tough one to take," he said. Liverpool face Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, the last game before the international break. They sit fifth with 15 points from nine games. Van Dijk said the clash with the Eagles is 'massive' after successive setbacks for Iraola's side. "It's massive. When we are back in Liverpool, preparing and recovering physically and mentally, we will be looking forward. It is always tough at Palace and I don't expect anything different." 'We cannot lose in the manner we did' The Dutchman believes the setbacks can still strengthen the squad. "I mentioned after the last game [against Arsenal] that we as a group have to go through good moments but also lesser good moments," he said. "That will only form a bigger bond and it will be only beneficial. No-one wants to lose games, especially how we did, but it should only help us in the near future. We should not accept losing, especially in the manner we did."

The Knights came into the game having already clinched their seventh straight district title, but Steele didn't rest on its laurels as it outscored Clemens 35-14 after the game was tied 7-7 early in the second quarter. Steele coach David Saenz said winning the district title for the seventh year in a row was a big accomplishment for the senior class, a group which hasn't lost a district game in four years. An East Central loss would secure Clemens' first playoff berth in seven years. The Hornets hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Buffaloes if it comes down to a two-way tie. Clemens coach Alan Hill said his team accomplished a lot in his third season as the Buffaloes' coach, as Clemens produced its first winning season in seven years. "It was really good," Hill said. item.title: Former Australia star Chris Lynn serves one-month ban after testing positive for cocaine on T20 Blast finals day
item.description: Northamptonshire Steelbacks batter Chris Lynn was handed, and served, a one month ban following a positive drug test for cocaine after the club won the T20 Vitality Blast final on July 18th. The Cricket Regulator confirmed that Lynn produced an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) following a drug test taken on Finals Day and an investigation was launched. Lynn’s urine sample was sent to the WADA -accredited Laboratory in the Laboratoire Anti-Dopage, France for analysis and returned Adverse Analytical Findings (“AAF”) for cocaine’s Metabolite benzoylecgonine meaning that it was a violation of cricket’s anti-doping rule. Cocaine is a substance banned “In Competition” but the investigation found that Lynn had taken the drug on the night of July 15th into the early hours of July 16th outside of competition. Northamptonshire won their Blast quarter-final against Gloucestershire that evening. Having also provided evidence supporting this position the regulator accepted that Lynn’s use of cocaine amounted to an out-of-competition ADR violation and was unrelated to sporting performance. The regulator charged Lynn with two ADR violations in September and sought a suspension of three months. The second of those violations – ADR Article 2.2 – in that the Cricketer Used a Prohibited Substance, namely cocaine, on or before 18 July 2026 (the “ADRVs”) – was withdrawn as the reported level of cocaine in the sample was below the minimum reporting level required. Lynn acknowledged and accepted the findings of the regulator and informed them of his decision to undergo a substance of abuse treatment programme. In October, the regulator received evidence that Lynn had completed the programme and his suspension was reduced to one month. That ban was served between Lynn’s provisional suspension on 31 July 2026 until 11.59pm on 30 August 2026. Northants beat Hampshire in the Vitality Blast T20 final at Edgbaston this year (PA) The findings also concluded that there was no requirement to inflict any sanction Northamptonshire Steelbacks. A statement from the Cricket Regulator reads: “The Cricket Regulator has imposed a one-month suspension on former Northamptonshire Steelbacks cricketer Chris Lynn. The period of suspension has now been served. “Mr Lynn produced an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) for the presence of cocaine's Metabolite, benzoylecgonine, related to an In Competition sample collected on the 18 July 2026. “Mr Lynn has accepted the sanction. No further comment will be made on this matter.”

item.title: Legendary Real Madrid forward sends message of support to Vinicius amid growing pressure
item.description: Legendary Real Madrid forward sends message of support to Vinicius amid growing pressure Vinicius Jr. has received public support from legendary Real Madrid teammate Karim Benzema in the wake of his struggle for consistency, growing criticism from fans, and increased competition for his place in the starting XI. Benzema shared a photograph of the two players together on Instagram, prompting Vinicius to repost the message on his own account. The gesture comes at a difficult moment for the 26-year-old, whose performances have attracted considerable scrutiny . Although Jose Mourinho and the club hierarchy continue to back him, his recent absence has coincided with an impressive run of results, while Yan Diomande has emerged as a serious competitor for his preferred position on the left wing. Benzema reminds Vinicius of the support he still has at Real Madrid Benzema’s message is quite significant for the Brazilian given the relationship the two forwards developed during their time together at Real Madrid. His Instagram message, which read, “N1 always”, appears to be an expression of confidence in his former teammate at a time when the Brazilian is facing considerable criticism. Vinicius acknowledged the gesture by sharing Benzema’s photograph and message on his own Instagram account. Diomande makes the most of Vinicius’ absence The challenge Vinicius is facing at Real Madrid is no longer limited to the fans, as his four-match LaLiga suspension has provided other players with opportunities to establish themselves. Crucially, Real Madrid have won all three league matches played during his domestic suspension, beating Sevilla 4-1, Barcelona 2-1 and Racing Santander 3-0. NFL commentator Skip Bayless used this opportunity to mock Baltimore’s decision to cut Diego Pavia after signing him as an undrafted free agent. item.description: Borussia Dortmund vs. SV Elversberg preview: Contrasting styles sets up epic clash Borussia Dortmund: With the final international break of 2027 just around the corner, Borussia Dortmund will be keen to go into the imposed rest on a high this weekend. On Saturday afternoon at 15:30 CET, they await the arrival of a newly promoted outfit SV Elversberg on Matchday 9. Dortmund managed to use last weekend's impressive 2-2 stalemate away to Bayern Munich in their favour midweek. A dominant yet momentarily jittery performance enabled them to defeat Real Betis on a 2-1 scoreline in Wednesday's Champions League encounter. The result appeared to come at a slight cost, however, for Niko Kovač's troops. Serhou Guirassy hobbled off, leaving him as a doubt for Saturday. Nonetheless, Fábio Silva will be ready to deputise having bagged yet another goal against their Andalusian opponents. Perhaps even more confidence-building is the fact Kostas Karetsas also scored. The Greek talent has been blighted by injuries, but opening the account will likely give his belief a major boost. BVB's solid rearguard also remains the best in the league, leaking just six. Emre Can and Giannis Konstantelias (both ACL tears) naturally won't feature, while Justin Lerma (muscle injury) is expected to remain out. SV Elversberg: As for the visitors, this is uncharted territory for SV Elversberg. They ride into town where they will get a taste of one of the Bundesliga's finest footballing temples. The biggest task thereafter is becoming quickly acclimatised to the atmosphere that often unnerves sides. It's no surprise that this is the first meeting of these two club's in Germany's topflight. The Saarland outfit's meteoric rise up the divisions presents an exciting clash. In ways, it's like a throwback given the visitors play a style akin to Jürgen Klopp's heavy metal era at BVB. A lot of that credit has to go to coach Vincent Wagner who, along with the Elversberg's chiefs, said they will show no fear and go after teams. That toe-to-toe battling style may just be exactly what could catch Dortmund cold on Saturday if they can make a fast start. Form has been somewhat turbulent in recent weeks for Elversberg. A crushing DFB-Pokal exit to SV Darmstadt (2-0) and thumping loss to RB Leipzig (4-0) left scars. Fortunately, they bounced back with a barnstorming 4-1 victory over Mainz to settle the nerves last Friday. item.description: Ireland begin their Nations Championship Northern Series campaign against Argentina on Friday [Getty Images] Los Pumas - two words to strike fear into the heart of Ireland rugby fans. As they return to the Aviva Stadium in the Nations Championship on Friday night, it feels something of an anomaly that a team who have inflicted so much hurt on Ireland over the years have never beaten them in Dublin. Indeed, out of the 20 previous meetings between these two sides, Ireland have won 14. It is the nature of those handful of losses, however, that have so coloured this rivalry. Three times the sides have met at the World Cup. Three times Argentina have won and three times the result has heralded Ireland's early exit from the competition. With Ireland's first game of Australia 2027 now just under 11 months away, the sight of the blue and white hoops of their frequent tournament nemesis will certainly sharpen the mind. All the more so given that, should results go in accordance with seeding, the sides would meet at the quarter-final stage on Halloween night in Brisbane. As he announced his team selection on Wednesday afternoon, Ireland head coach Andy Farrell acknowledged his side are not presently "good enough to board the plane believing that 100%" they are ready to lift the Webb Ellis trophy for the first time. A year out from the World Cups of 2015, 2019 and 2023, Ireland had enjoyed banner seasons, and by this stage were eagerly anticipating the tournaments to come. While that has not been the case through 2026 to date, the head coach added that he is excited by the thought of the work still to do. If wider optimism around next year feels in short supply, it is because Ireland's issues have come to bear when playing the very best. Across the past two years, their only six defeats have come in the six games they have played against New Zealand, South Africa and France. All came via double-digit scores. As such, the eye has long been drawn to the visit of the Springboks to Dublin on 21 November, but there can be no looking past a dangerous Argentina fixture. The Pumas will be expected to provide a good yardstick for both the collective and a number of individuals in an intriguing selection. With Jack Crowley injured, Sam Prendergast has another opportunity to grab the 10 jersey.
